name: VGA Sixteen
summary: A site that looks like the thing it is about: sixteen colours, hard edges, thick borders, windows on a desk. Every colour is one of the 16 VGA colours and the build refuses any other. Blue panels carry their own light-on-blue colours in both colour schemes.

intent.mood: bold, retro, exact, a little playful
for: sites about a retro system, a language or a machine with a fixed palette
pages whose identity is a constraint (a palette, a screen size)
study sites whose facts are of uneven reliability
not_for: subjects with no visual constraint to honour
pages that need subtle colour (charts with many hues)

pairs.role: text secondary on a blue panel
text accent on a blue panel
text link on a blue panel

type.display: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", "JetBrains Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace
type.text: system-ui, -apple-system, "Segoe UI", Roboto, "Helvetica Neue", Arial, sans-serif
type.mono: ui-monospace, "SF Mono", "Cascadia Mono", "JetBrains Mono", Menlo, Consolas, monospace

shape.note: no rounding, no gradients, no transparency, no shadows; thick 4 to 8 px borders in light grey; every colour in the stylesheet is one of the 16, enforced by the build

signature.name: the screen
signature.rule: A bezeled blue window with a light-grey title bar reading the display mode, holding a pixel-art logo drawn from bitmap letters (one palette colour per letter), a tagline, a real program and its real output with a block cursor. Every inner page opens as a smaller version of the same window, with a title bar carrying the page's name. A thin bar of all 16 colours, with their names and numbers, sits below.
signature.carries: the display the subject runs on: its resolution, its full palette with names and indices, and a real program with its real output
signature.derived_from: data/palette.json (the colours, names and indices), data/hero.json and the recorded interpreter output

motifs.rule: Every colour value is one of the 16; no rgba, hsl, gradient, opacity or filter. A build step reads the stylesheet and refuses to continue otherwise.
Panels are blue in both colour schemes and re-scope their own custom properties to light-on-blue, so the light page is a white desk and the dark page a black one, with the same windows on both.

A rule style plus a word: solid Firm, dashed Reported, dotted Uncertain. The definition of the top mark says what was and was not checked ('not checked against a source here'), and a one-line legend sits above every list of marked facts. 'Reported' is explained as not meaning doubted.

motifs.use: any output that did not come from the real system
motifs.rule: Say where an output came from, where it is shown: 'Output from this site's interpreter (a subset of HolyC), not from TempleOS.'

never: a colour outside the palette, or a gradient or transparency
white text on a panel that goes white in another scheme or in print (re-scope the colours per panel and force black on white for print)
a top confidence mark whose definition promises a check that has not happened
an output shown on a themed screen without saying it did not come from the real system
ordering the facts of a sensitive subject so that the most sensational come first
a causal claim about a person's illness that no source in hand supports

provenance.source_run: SolutionsAsService/HolyC, Adaptive Full run bounded to one panel round (Arnheim, Krug, Debord, Cairo); see its DESIGN-LOG.md
measured: Mobile Floor 12 of 12 on all six pages at 360, 390 and 430px
contrast walk: 214 distinct text and background pairs across the six pages in both colour schemes, none under threshold
rendered landing: 16 of 16 palette colours and no off-palette colour apart from anti-aliasing (Cairo)
palette enforced by the build: 16 colour values in the stylesheet, all from the 16
open: one panel round; S1 and S2 not met
all facts from general knowledge, none sourced
outputs from a site-written interpreter checked against C, not against the real system
not shown on a real phone
